options.label: change no file

The header, the Overview and the embedded summary in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md say nothing about the request entry or a separate command, so nothing they hold is false. The clause is corrected, if at all, by the phase plan's owning skill.

The edit would break the Touch rule and the dispatch's explicit 'Do not edit the node's ## Phase Plan'.

why: Every sentence Q-081 names is in the Phase Plan (simple-login.integration.3 Scope (b)); grep finds no mention of the request entry or a separate command in the header, the Overview or the parent's embedded summary. hsdd-spec Touch: 'Never edit the node's ## Phase Plan, except under the Citation touch paragraph', and that paragraph applies only when a source moves to a new version or a contract version is superseded; booking-api@v1 is stable, current and not deprecated. The header and Overview stay true after S21's answer. A header or Overview sentence that named the request or the fallback would have required the edit.

question: Q-081: since this touch may not edit the Phase Plan (DEC-220), does the stale clause in simple-login.integration.3 Scope (b) get a step of its own in this run, or wait for a later touch of the phase?

options.label: route an insert-step: phase-plan-append on simple-login.integration rewriting simple-login.integration.3 in place
options.consequence: One more step, wording only. Scope (b)'s assumption sentence cites booking-api@v1's Development address (the service creates its tables in the existing empty database DATABASE_URL names before it listens; the rooms are part of the service and need no loading) and the separate-command fallback goes. The phase keeps its id, name, tier, size, gate, consumes and dependencies, and its work is unchanged, so no pending entry and no reconcile are expected. The unshipped full-review phase reaches its OpenSpec cycle with no dangling pointer.

options.label: close as explained with no step
options.consequence: No cost now. The clause stays: it names a request entry the Governance updates section no longer holds, offers a branch the producer's answer closed, and says the service creates 'the four pre-loaded rooms' in the database where the contract says the rooms are not rows. The implementer resolves it from booking-api@v1, which the phase consumes. No later step of this run touches the node: the align skips leaf-parents the segment re-planned, so the fix waits for a future segment, possibly after the phase is built.

options.label: route a consider back to simple-login.integration
options.consequence: The consistency stage dispatches a step per open item, so it would come back as another spec-touch facing the same Phase Plan rule: a loop that fixes nothing.

chosen: route an insert-step: phase-plan-append on simple-login.integration rewriting simple-login.integration.3 in place
why: Only hsdd-phase-plan may change a phase's Scope, and simple-login.integration.3 is unshipped (no hsdd/verify/simple-login.integration.3.verification.md on main), so its Scope is the input its OpenSpec cycle reads. The sentence is false twice after S21: the request entry is drained, and a separate command will not come (DEC-198); it also says the service creates the rooms in the database, which booking-api@v1's Development address contradicts. The intake record's insert rule does not require this step, since nothing the phase implements, consumes or replays changes; that is why this is routed as a proposal for the orchestrator to accept or reject rather than claimed under the rule. The options are close: S21 judged 'a later touch' enough. A planned later phase-plan pass on simple-login.integration in this segment, or a run budget that admits only rule-driven inserts, would have made closing with no step the choice.
